- A machine can process at most one task at a time.
- You must assign a start time to every task so that all machine conflicts are avoided.
- Use the task order as provided in the instance.

Objective:
- Minimize the makespan (the completion time of the last finishing task).

You will receive the instance below:
{{INSTANCE_INPUT}}

Return your schedule using exactly the following JSON format (no extra keys, no explanations):
```json
{
  "solution": [
    {
      "job": <job_id>,
      "tasks": [
        {
          "task": <task_index>,
          "start": <start_time>,
          "machine": <machine_id>,
          "duration": <duration>
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```
Rules:
- Include every job exactly once in the outer list.
- For each job, include all of its tasks exactly once.
- The `machine` and `duration` must match the instance for that job/task.
- Start times must produce a valid schedule (no machine overlap).
- Use identifiers exactly as they appear in the input.
**Do not include explanations or any extra keys.**

contexts.text: [BASELINE] Canonical task wording.

As the bakery shift leader, arrange when each batch moves through the fixed row of stations with known processing times so no station handles multiple steps at the same time, and aim to have all batches finished as early as possible.

As the print shop coordinator, schedule the start times for every print run through the predetermined sequence of machines with given task lengths, ensuring no machine processes multiple runs simultaneously, and minimize the moment when all print jobs are complete.

As the car detailer in charge, plan the order and timing for each vehicle to pass through the fixed sequence of service bays with known step durations, make sure no bay works on several steps at the same time, and try to reduce the time until every vehicle is done.

As the laundry manager, decide the timetable for garments to flow through the fixed list of care stations with specified operation lengths, ensure that no station treats more than a single operation at once, and keep the overall completion time for all garments as small as possible.

As the electronics assembly supervisor, set start times for each circuit board to move through the established line of workstations with known task durations, forbid any workstation from handling multiple tasks concurrently, and minimize the finishing time for the whole batch.

As the small bakery owner, sequence and time each cookie tray through the fixed set of ovens and cooling areas with given processing durations, prevent any area from working on several trays at the same time, and aim to have all trays completed as soon as possible.

As the film post producer, assign when each scene clip should go through the set sequence of editing stations with known processing lengths, avoid having any station work on multiple clips at once, and minimize the overall time until all clips are finalized.

As the catering line lead, plan when each dish moves through the established cooking and finishing stations with known task times, ensure no station tackles multiple dish steps at the same time, and strive to finish the entire meal service as quickly as possible.

As the lab technician, schedule start times for every sample as it passes through the fixed order of instruments with specified analysis durations, make sure no instrument runs multiple analyses simultaneously, and minimize the time when all samples have been processed.

As the furniture shop foreperson, decide the sequence and timing for each table to go through the fixed sequence of work centers with given operation lengths, prevent any center from handling multiple operations at the same time, and aim to complete the entire set in the shortest possible span.

As the small brewery operator, organize when each batch moves through the fixed series of tanks and conditioning steps with specified processing times, stop any tank from serving multiple batches at once, and minimize the time by which all batches are ready.

As the auto body shop manager, determine the schedule for each vehicle to follow the set sequence of repair bays with known task durations, ensure that no bay works on more than a single repair activity simultaneously, and minimize the completion time for the whole set of vehicles.

As the bakery line planner, control the timing of each dough piece through the fixed procession of machines with given processing durations, prohibit any machine from running multiple pieces at the same time, and aim to reduce the total time until every piece is finished.

As the packaging shift supervisor, plan when each parcel moves through the fixed order of packing stations with established task lengths, prevent stations from handling multiple parcels at once, and minimize the time when all parcels have been packed.

As the ceramics kiln scheduler, assign start times for each pot to travel through the fixed sequence of preparation, drying, and firing stations with known durations, make sure no station is processing several pots concurrently, and strive to minimize the time when the entire set is completed.

As the electronics test supervisor, set the schedule for each device to go through the fixed sequence of tests with specified durations, ensure no test bench runs more than one test at a time, and minimize the moment when all devices have completed testing.

As the car wash supervisor, plan vehicle passages so every vehicle follows prewash, soap, rinse, and drying in the identical order and no bay serves overlapping vehicles, so that the whole group of vehicles is done as quickly as possible.

As the salon manager, book client flows so each client proceeds through shampoo, cutting, and styling in the same progression and no stylist attends overlapping clients, with the aim of finishing all appointments in the minimum total time.

As the photo lab lead, order print jobs so every print goes through exposure, developing, and drying in the same sequence and no machine handles overlapping jobs, with the objective of completing the entire batch as quickly as possible.

As the electronics line coordinator, schedule circuit boards through soldering, testing, and final packing in the identical station order while preventing any station from working on overlapping boards, in order to minimize the time until the full set is complete.

As the clinic receptionist, space patient slots so each patient visits registration, sample collection, and analysis in the same sequence and no diagnostic instrument serves overlapping patients, with the goal of having all patients finished as soon as possible.

As the coffee shop shift lead, plan drink preparations so each order passes through espresso extraction, milk steaming, and final assembly in the same order and no piece of equipment is used by overlapping orders, aiming to get the whole batch of orders done quickly.

As the print shop manager, sequence document runs so every job moves through layout, printing, and binding in the identical order and no press or binder accepts overlapping jobs, with the aim of minimizing the completion time for the full set.

As the pottery studio instructor, plan kiln and bench time so every vessel follows shaping, drying, and firing in the same progression and no bench or kiln processes overlapping pieces, with the objective of finishing the whole collection as quickly as possible.

As the phone repair team lead, assign devices so each device passes through inspection, repair, and testing in the same sequence and no workstation handles overlapping devices, aiming to complete the entire batch of repairs in minimal total time.

As the bike shop supervisor, schedule services so each bicycle goes through inspection, adjustment, and road check in the same order and no service bay handles overlapping bikes, with the goal of having all bikes ready as soon as possible.

As the dry cleaner owner, plan garment processing so every item follows stain treatment, cleaning, and pressing in the identical sequence and no machine processes overlapping garments, so the full load is finished in the shortest time.

As the small studio producer, organize footage so each scene moves through shooting, rough edit, and color grading in the same sequence and no editing suite works on overlapping scenes, with the aim of completing the whole shoot package as quickly as possible.

As the science lab teacher, stagger student groups so each group proceeds through setup, experimentation, and cleanup in the same progression and no bench hosts overlapping groups, with the objective of concluding all experiments in minimal total time.

As the nursery manager, plan sapling processing so each plant passes through potting, fertilizing, and shading in the same order and no workstation tends overlapping plants, with the goal of finishing the whole batch in the least possible time.

As the pizza shop shift manager, coordinate pies so each pizza follows dough shaping, topping, and baking in the identical station order and no station handles overlapping pizzas, so that all pizzas are finished in the shortest overall time.

As the auto shop owner, plan the sequence of customer vehicles so that every vehicle goes through inspection, repair, and paint in the identical order with given service durations, prevent any service bay from handling overlapping cars, and minimize the time when the last vehicle is completed.

As the tailor in charge, plan garment work so that every garment goes through cutting, stitching, and pressing in the identical workflow with known operation times, ensure workstations do not process overlapping pieces, and complete the entire batch as soon as possible.

As the clinic administrator, schedule patient imaging so that each patient proceeds through registration, scanning, and review in the same order with expected durations for each stage, prevent any scanner or room from serving multiple patients at once, and shorten the time until every patient’s visit is finished.

As the woodshop foreperson, sequence workpieces so that each piece undergoes cutting, sanding, and varnishing in the same fixed order with known operation times, ensure no tool station processes overlapping pieces, and complete the full set of pieces as soon as possible.

As the upholstery shop manager, plan furniture pieces so that each frame goes through cutting, assembly, and stitching in the identical workflow with known task lengths, avoid simultaneous processing of a station by multiple frames, and minimize the time when the final piece is ready.

As the small factory supervisor, plan product batches so that each item follows stamping, assembly, and inspection in the same order with known operation times, prevent any machine from working on overlapping items, and get the entire production run finished as early as possible.

As the shipping center lead, sequence parcels so that every parcel goes through scanning, labeling, and sorting in the same prescribed order with known handling times, ensure workstations do not handle overlapping parcels, and minimize the time until the last parcel is ready for dispatch.

As the software build coordinator, organize code changes so that each change moves through compile, test, and deploy in the same pipeline order with predictable step durations, ensure build agents are not running overlapping tasks, and minimize the time until the final change is fully deployed.

As the food cannery supervisor, plan production so that every can follows sterilization, filling, and sealing in the same fixed sequence with known processing times, prevent any line segment from processing overlapping cans, and finish the entire batch as soon as possible.

As the repair shop coordinator for small appliances, schedule units so that each unit goes through diagnosis, parts replacement, and final testing in the same workflow with known durations per task, make sure no bench handles overlapping units, and minimize the time when the last unit is ready for pickup.

As the home cook, plan when to move each casserole through the same sequence of prep, oven, and cooling so that every dish is finished as soon as possible while ensuring no appliance handles multiple casseroles at the same time.

As the baker, schedule each loaf through the shared pathway of mixing, baking, and glazing to have all loaves ready in the least possible time, and do not let any equipment operate on more than one loaf simultaneously.

As the press operator, schedule booklets through printing, trimming, and binding along the identical workflow to keep the overall completion time minimal, ensuring each machine processes only one batch at a time.

As the roastery manager, line up green bean loads through roasting, cooling, and packing in the common sequence so the entire run completes in the shortest possible time, and ensure no machine processes multiple loads concurrently.

As the plant supervisor, schedule plastic pieces through the consistent stages of molding, trimming, and inspection to minimize the time when all pieces are finished, and do not allow any station to work on more than one piece at once.

As the catering coordinator, plan how each platter moves through assembly, chilling, and staging in the same order so that all platters are ready as quickly as possible, with each station handling only one platter at a time.

As the cafeteria manager, assign when trays pass through prep, warming, and serving along the common route to get every tray completed as soon as possible, ensuring no station serves multiple trays simultaneously.

As the craftsman, arrange the sequence in which tabletops go through cutting, sanding, and finishing so the whole lot is completed in the shortest time, and avoid having any machine work on more than one tabletop concurrently.

As the lab manager, schedule biological samples through centrifuge, incubation, and assay in the same prescribed order so that all samples are processed as quickly as possible, with no piece of equipment running multiple samples at once.

As the line supervisor, time how toys travel through priming, painting, and varnishing along the identical production route so the entire set is completed in the least amount of time, and keep each station focused on only one toy at a time.

As the assembly supervisor, plan the progression of phones through screen fitting, casing press, and final check in the same order to minimize the moment when the last phone is finished, ensuring each workstation handles only a single handset at a time.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total count of dough batches the shift must process through the fixed line of stations. This is the number of jobs to schedule so the last completion time (makespan) is minimized.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of distinct processing stations in the bakery row (e.g., mixing, proofing, baking, cooling). All batches visit these stations in the same order; each station can handle at most one batch at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for each batch that must be scheduled. Each identifier represents one job that will sequentially visit every station in the fixed order.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the stations in the fixed processing order. These identify which physical station a task requires when scheduling a batch's step.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the batch this task belongs to (matches one entry from batch_ids). Used to group the sequence of steps that must be performed in order for that batch.

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Index of the step within the batch's sequence (e.g., 1 for first station, 2 for second). Steps must be executed in increasing step_index order for each batch.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the station required for this step (must match one of the station_ids). Indicates which station the batch must occupy during this step, respecting the single-batch-at-a-time constraint.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Time the batch spends at the given station for this step (in consistent time units, e.g., minutes). This is the deterministic processing time used to compute start/end times and the overall makespan.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of separate print jobs (print runs) in this batch to schedule. An integer count used to size the schedule and iterate over jobs.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of distinct processing stations (machines) in the common sequence every job must visit. This equals the length of the machine sequence and determines how many operations each job has.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of identifiers for the print jobs (IDs or names). These identifiers are referenced by each task to indicate which job the operation belongs to.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: The ordered list of machine/station identifiers representing the common processing route (first machine through last machine) that every job follows.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the print job this specific operation belongs to; must match one of the entries in the 'print_job_ids' list.

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The position of this operation in the job's sequence (operation order). A smaller index means the operation must be performed earlier for that job.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the machine/station required to perform this operation; must correspond to one of the 'machine_ids' in the shared machine order.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The time the operation occupies its machine (in consistent time units across the instance). Used to compute operation finish times and the overall makespan.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of vehicles (cars) that must be scheduled to pass through the detail line. As the lead detailer, this tells you how many jobs need ordering and timing.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of distinct service bays (machines) in the fixed processing sequence that every vehicle must visit. Each bay can handle at most one vehicle at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for each vehicle to schedule (e.g., ticket numbers or license plates). Use these IDs when assigning an order and start/finish times for each car.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Ordered list of identifiers for the service bays (e.g., 'wash', 'dry', 'vacuum') representing the common sequence every vehicle must follow.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the vehicle for this specific task; must match one entry from vehicle_ids.

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Position of this treatment step within the vehicle's fixed sequence (1 = first bay, 2 = second, etc.), defining the required order of visits.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the service bay required to perform this step; must match one entry from service_bay_ids and indicates which bay will be occupied for the given duration.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Time required (in the chosen time units, e.g., minutes) for the specified bay to complete this treatment on the vehicle.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of garments to schedule through the laundry line (each garment is a job: e.g., a particular shirt, dress, or towel).

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of care stations in the fixed processing sequence (machines), i.e., how many distinct steps each garment must pass through.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Ordered list or set of identifiers for each garment to be processed (job labels used when assigning operations to time slots).

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Ordered list of identifiers for the care stations (machines) that form the common route every garment follows (e.g., wash, rinse, dry, press).

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the garment that this task belongs to (must match one entry in 'garment_ids').

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Position index of this operation within the garment's sequence (1 means first station visit, 2 the second, etc.), reflecting the fixed order of stations.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the care station required for this operation; must match one of the entries in 'station_ids' and indicates which station will be occupied for the given duration.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Processing time required for this garment at the specified station (in consistent time units); this is how long the station is occupied for that task.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of circuit boards in the batch that must pass through the assembly line; the supervisor must schedule all of these boards.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of distinct workstations (stations on the line). Each workstation can process at most one board at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifiers for each circuit board in the batch (one identifier per board) used to refer to that board's sequence of steps.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifiers for the workstations in the line (used to specify which workstation a task requires); the order of workstations is the common machine order for all boards.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the circuit board that this task belongs to (matches one entry from board_ids).

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The position of this processing step within the board's required sequence (1-based index of the step that must be performed in order).

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Which workstation (from workstation_ids) is required for this step of the board; indicates the resource that will be occupied during the step.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: How long the board occupies the specified workstation for this step (time units); used by the supervisor to compute start and end times and to avoid overlapping use of the same workstation.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total count of cookie trays (jobs) that must each pass through the full sequence of ovens and cooling areas; used to know how many trays to schedule.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of distinct processing areas (machines) in the fixed sequence (e.g., Oven1, Oven2, Cooler); each station can handle at most one tray at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for each tray (job) to be scheduled. These IDs link each tray to its sequence of tasks and are used to report start/finish times per tray.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Ordered list of the processing area identifiers (ovens and cooling areas) shared by all trays; the order here is the common routing every tray must follow.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the tray this task belongs to; must match one entry from the global tray_identifiers list.

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Position of this task in the tray's fixed processing sequence (1 = first station, 2 = second, etc.); enforces the order trays must follow without skipping or reordering steps.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the required station (oven or cooler) for this task; must match one entry from the global station_identifiers and reflects which area the tray occupies for this step.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Time required for this tray at the given station (e.g., minutes in an oven or minutes to cool); used to compute start/finish times and ultimately the makespan.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of film clips in the batch that must be scheduled through the post‑production workflow (equivalent to the number of jobs).

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of editing bays/stations in the fixed sequence that every clip must visit (equivalent to the number of machines).

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers (names or IDs) for each clip in the batch. These IDs are referenced by the per‑task entries to assign tasks to specific clips.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the editing bays/stations in the fixed processing order. Task entries refer to these IDs to indicate which bay a step requires.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the clip that this task belongs to (must match one of the entries in the global 'clip_ids').

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The position of this processing step within the clip's sequence (an index indicating the order the clip visits the bays; steps are executed in increasing index order and cannot be skipped or repeated).

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the editing bay required for this step (must match one of the global 'bay_ids'); each bay can process at most one clip at a time.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The time required for this clip's step on the specified bay, expressed in the instance's consistent time unit. Used to compute start/finish times when scheduling to minimize the overall completion time.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total count of distinct dishes (jobs) that must pass through the catering line during the service; used to know how many job schedules to produce.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Total count of cooking/finishing stations in the fixed sequence (e.g., prep, cook, plating); every dish visits these stations in the same order.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers (names or IDs) for each dish to be scheduled; each identifier corresponds to one job moving through the stations.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Ordered list of station identifiers representing the cooking/finishing stations in the exact sequence all dishes follow.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the dish (matches an entry from dish_identifiers) to which this task/step belongs.

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Sequence index of the step within the dish's process (1st step, 2nd step, ...); indicates order the dish must follow through stations.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the specific station required for this step (must match one of the station_identifiers); ensures the task is assigned to the correct station in the sequence.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Fixed processing time (e.g., in minutes) that the dish occupies the specified station for this step; used to compute start/finish times and avoid overlapping station use.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of samples (jobs) that must be processed through the instrument lineup. This tells the scheduler how many job sequences need start times assigned.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of distinct instruments (machines) in the fixed processing sequence. Each instrument can run at most one analysis at a time and this count defines the length of every sample's workflow.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the samples to be scheduled. Each identifier corresponds to one job for which you must plan start times on every instrument.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Ordered list of instrument identifiers representing the fixed processing order shared by all samples; the k-th instrument here is the machine used for every sample's k-th step.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the sample that this task belongs to; must match one of the entries in sample_ids and ties the task into that sample's workflow.

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Position index of this task within the sample's ordered sequence of analyses (i.e., which step of the fixed instrument order this is). The scheduler must preserve this order for each sample.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the instrument required for this task; must correspond to one of instrument_ids and indicates which instrument must be reserved for the given step of the sample.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Processing time required for this task on the specified instrument (in the same time units used for the schedule). The scheduler must allocate this contiguous time on the instrument and cannot overlap it with other tasks on the same instrument.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of tabletops (jobs) in the current batch — how many separate pieces must each pass through the full sequence of stations and therefore how many job sequences you must schedule.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of physical work centers (stations) in the fixed processing route (for this shop: sanding, staining, assembly); each station can process at most one table at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifiers for each tabletop job (e.g., T1, T2, ...) — the list of items to be ordered and scheduled through the stations.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifiers for each station in the processing order (e.g., sanding, staining, assembly) that correspond to the physical machines where tasks run.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the specific tabletop job this task belongs to (must match one of the entries in 'table_ids').

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The position of this operation inside the table's fixed sequence of steps (1 = first step, 2 = second, etc.), enforcing the required processing order (sanding → staining → assembly).

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the station (from 'station_ids') required for this operation; used to ensure the task is scheduled on the correct physical work center and to prevent overlapping use.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The known time length for this operation on the specified station (e.g., minutes); used to compute start and end times for the task and to evaluate the makespan.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of beer lots (batches) that must be processed through the brewery line this morning. This is the count of distinct jobs to schedule.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of sequential processing stages (tanks and finishing/conditioning steps) that every batch must pass through in the same fixed order.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifiers (labels) for each batch/lot to be scheduled (e.g., Batch1, LotA). These correspond to the nr_batches items to be sequenced through the stages.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifiers for each tank or finishing stage in the fixed processing lineup (e.g., MashTank, Fermenter1, Conditioning). These define the ordered machines/stations used by all batches.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the batch/lot this task belongs to (matches one entry from batch_ids).

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The position index of this task within the batch's sequence (1..nr_stages), indicating which step in the fixed order this task represents.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the required tank or finishing stage for this task (matches one entry from stage_ids); each task must be processed on this specific stage.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The time the batch occupies the specified tank/stage for this task (in the same time units used by the instance). This is the blocking duration during which that stage cannot serve other batches.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total count of vehicles in the current batch that must pass through the repair workflow; this is the number of separate repair jobs to schedule.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of distinct repair bays (service stations) in the shop that vehicles must visit in sequence; each bay can service at most one vehicle at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for each vehicle in the batch (e.g., VINs, job numbers); these identify each repair job to be scheduled through the bays.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the repair bays (e.g., 'Body', 'Paint', 'Electrical' or numeric bay numbers); these define the ordered stations that every vehicle will visit.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the vehicle to which this task belongs; must match one entry from vehicle_ids and associates the task with that car's repair job.

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Position index of this service step within the vehicle's fixed sequence of repair operations (first step = 1, second = 2, etc.), indicating order of tasks that cannot be skipped or reordered for that vehicle.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the repair bay required for this specific service step; must match one of the bay_ids and indicates which station must process the vehicle at this step.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Processing time required for this vehicle at the specified bay (in consistent time units, e.g., minutes); the bay will be occupied for this duration when servicing the vehicle.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of dough pieces (jobs) that must pass through the bakery line. This is the count of distinct items to schedule; the planner must ensure every piece completes every operation in sequence.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of physical machines or workstations in the fixed procession (the length of the processing chain). Each station can process at most one dough piece at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for each dough piece to be scheduled (one identifier per job). These IDs refer to distinct pieces whose operations must be ordered and timed through the line.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the machines/stations in the production chain (the same order applies to all pieces). These IDs are used to refer to which station a given task requires.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the dough piece (job) that this task belongs to. Matches one entry from dough_piece_ids and ties the task to that piece's sequence of operations.

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Position index of the operation within the dough piece's fixed processing sequence (typically 1..nr_stations). Defines the precedence order: operation_index k must finish before k+1 starts for the same piece.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the station (machine) where this operation must be processed. It must match one of the station_ids and indicates which physical resource cannot be shared at overlapping times.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Processing time required for this operation on its required station, expressed in consistent time units (e.g., minutes). This is the continuous time the station is occupied by this dough piece for that operation.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of parcels that must be packed during the shift — each parcel is a job that must visit every packing station in the fixed order. This sets the number of job records the schedule must include.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of packing stations in the fixed processing lineup. Every parcel must pass through these stations in this order; this value determines how many processing steps each parcel has.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: The identifiers for the parcels to schedule (e.g., parcel numbers). Each identifier corresponds to one job that needs the full sequence of station tasks.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifiers for the packing stations, listed in the fixed processing order (first station to last). These identifiers are referenced by each parcel's tasks to indicate where they are processed.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the parcel for this task entry; matches one of the values in parcel_ids so the task can be assigned to the correct parcel.

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The position index of this task in the parcel's processing sequence (e.g., 1..nr_stations). It indicates which step of the ordered station sequence this task represents.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Which packing station processes this task; must match one of the station_ids and corresponds to the station at the given station_step_index in the fixed order.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Time required (in the schedule's time units) for the parcel to be processed at the specified station. This is the service time that blocks the station while that parcel is being packed.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total count of pots that must be processed through the kiln workflow. The scheduler must assign start times for each of these pots at each station.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of distinct processing stations in the fixed sequence (prep, dry, fire). This is the number of places that can process at most one pot at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for each pot (job). Each identifier uniquely names a pot that will pass through the prep→dry→fire sequence.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the stations (machines). These correspond to the preparation, drying, and firing stations used in the fixed order.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the pot that this task belongs to (must match an entry from pot_ids).

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Position of the task in the pot's sequence (1 = prep, 2 = dry, 3 = fire). All pots share the same ordered stages.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the station required for this stage (must match an entry from station_ids), e.g., prep, dry, or fire.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Time needed for the pot to be processed at this station (in the instance's time units). The station is occupied for this full duration and cannot handle another pot simultaneously.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of devices that need to be tested (the count of jobs to schedule across all test benches).

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct test benches (machines) that each device must visit in the fixed test sequence.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for each device to be tested (unique IDs for the jobs to be scheduled).

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for each test bench (machine) in the lab, ordered or referenced when assigning specific tests.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the device to which this test task belongs (matches one entry from device_identifiers).

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Position of this test in the device's fixed sequence of tests (the index of the test step within the job's ordered workflow).

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the test bench required for this test step (matches one entry from test_bench_identifiers).

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Time required for the device to complete this test on the specified test bench (use the same time unit for all tasks).

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of vehicles to schedule through the car wash. This equals the length of the vehicle list and tells you how many vehicle jobs must be sequenced.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of distinct wash stations (bays) in the required processing sequence (e.g., prewash, soap, rinse, drying). Every vehicle must visit these stations in the same order; this number defines how many sequential steps each vehicle has.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifiers for each vehicle (ticket number, plate, or index). Use these IDs to refer to individual vehicles when listing their sequence of steps and scheduling them through the stations.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifiers for the wash stations (e.g., 'prewash', 'soap', 'rinse', 'drying' or numeric bay IDs) in the common processing order. Tasks reference these IDs to indicate which station they require.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The vehicle identifier that this task belongs to (must match one of the vehicle_ids). Associates each processing step with the specific vehicle being washed.

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The position of this task in the vehicle's required sequence (1 = first step, 2 = second, etc.). In this scenario step indices correspond to the ordered stages each vehicle must pass through (prewash → soap → rinse → drying).

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the wash station (one of station_ids) required for this task. Each task must be processed at its specified station, and a station can only serve one vehicle at a time.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The processing time required at that station for this vehicle's step, expressed in the scheduling time unit (e.g., minutes). This is the time the station will be occupied and cannot overlap with other tasks at the same station.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of clients to schedule. Each client is a job that must visit shampoo, cutting, and styling in that order.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of distinct sequential service stations (processing steps) in the salon workflow — here the fixed sequence of services such as shampoo, cutting, and styling.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for each client to be booked. Each identifier refers to one client's full sequence of three services.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the service stations in processing order (e.g., shampoo_station, cutting_chair, styling_station). These define the machine types each service step requires.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the client that this task belongs to (matches one entry in client_ids).

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Index of the service within the client's sequence (e.g., 1 = shampoo, 2 = cutting, 3 = styling). This enforces the required order each client must follow.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the specific station type required for this task (must match one of station_ids), e.g., which shampoo sink, cutting chair, or styling station is needed.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Time in minutes required for this client to be processed at the given station. Used to ensure stations are not double-booked and to compute the overall finishing time.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of print jobs in the batch — an integer count of individual prints that must pass through the lab pipeline (exposure → developing → drying).

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of distinct processing stations (machines) in the fixed pipeline. In this lab scenario this corresponds to the stages exposure, developing, drying (commonly 3), but stated generally as the count of ordered stations.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for each print job (e.g., P1, P2, ...). These IDs are used to refer to each print when building the schedule and associating its sequence of tasks.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the processing stations in the common order (for example ['exposure','developing','drying']). Every print follows this same ordered list when being scheduled.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the print this task belongs to — must match one entry from the 'print_ids' list. Used to group a print's tasks and enforce their order through the pipeline.

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The position of this task in the print's processing sequence (an integer index). In the lab context 1 = exposure, 2 = developing, 3 = drying (or more generally 1..nr_stations), and tasks for a print must execute in increasing step_index.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the station/machine required for this task — must match one entry from 'station_ids' and indicates which lab station (exposure, developing, drying) will process this task.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Processing time required for this print at the specified station, in the chosen time unit (e.g., minutes). These durations drive the schedule: stations cannot process overlapping tasks and the solver uses these to minimize the time when the last print finishes drying (the makespan).

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of circuit boards that must pass through the line (each is a job to be scheduled).

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of work stations in the identical processing order (for this scenario: soldering, testing, packing — typically 3).

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of unique identifiers for each circuit board to be scheduled; these tie together the sequence of steps for that board.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Ordered list of station identifiers representing the line sequence (first soldering station id, then testing station id, then packing station id).

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the circuit board this task belongs to (must match an entry from board_ids).

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Index of the step within the board's required sequence (1 = soldering, 2 = testing, 3 = packing, matching the station order).

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the station required for this step (must match one of the station_ids and indicates soldering/testing/packing as appropriate).

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The time the board needs at this station for the given step (non‑negative); used to compute start/end times and the overall makespan.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of patients the receptionist must schedule through the clinic (each patient is a job that needs all three stops).

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of distinct service points (e.g., registration desk, sample collection area, diagnostic instrument) that patients must visit in the same order.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: The identifiers for each patient to be scheduled (one entry per patient), used to track their sequence of visits through the clinic.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: The identifiers for each clinic station or device (e.g., check-in, sample collection, analysis) that cannot serve more than one patient at a time.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the patient who needs the task (ties a specific visit to that patient).

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The position of this visit within the patient's required sequence (1 = check-in, 2 = sample collection, 3 = diagnostics); tasks must occur in this order for each patient.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Which clinic station or device the step requires (e.g., registration desk, collection bay, diagnostic instrument) and therefore which resource must be reserved for that time.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: How long that patient’s visit to the specified station takes (e.g., minutes); used to determine start/end times and to ensure no two patients overlap on the same station.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of drink orders in the current batch that must be prepared. The schedule must include exactly this many orders to route through the three-step workflow.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of distinct pieces of equipment/stations available (e.g., espresso machine, milk steamer, assembly table). Each station can handle at most one order at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifiers for each drink order (e.g., order IDs). These are the job labels the solver will sequence through the workflow.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifiers for each station/equipment (e.g., 'espresso', 'steamer', 'assembly'). Tasks reference these identifiers to indicate which piece of equipment they need.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the drink order this task belongs to (matches one entry from orders_list).

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Index of the preparation step within the order's fixed sequence. Under the café workflow this reflects the position in the espresso→milk→assembly sequence (0 = espresso extraction, 1 = milk steaming, 2 = final assembly). Tasks for an order must occur in increasing step_index order.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Which station/equipment the step requires (must match one entry from stations_list), e.g., espresso machine for step_index 0, steamer for step_index 1, assembly table for step_index 2. Each station can process only one step at a time.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Processing time required for this step for the given order (in the same time units used across the instance). This is the time the order occupies the specified station when that step is scheduled.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of document runs (jobs) that must pass through layout, printing, and binding; the number of separate pieces/orders to schedule.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct workstations or machines in the shop (e.g., layout station(s), printing press(es), binder(s)) that can perform tasks; each machine can handle at most one task at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for each document run (e.g., job names or numbers). Each identifier corresponds to one job that must go through the three stages in order.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Ordered list of machine identifiers representing the sequence of stages every job follows (layout, printing, binding). Each identifier names a specific workstation (e.g., Layout1, Press2, BinderA).

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the document run this task belongs to (one of the entries from job_ids).

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Index of the task within the job's fixed sequence of stages (1 = layout, 2 = printing, 3 = binding); reflects the required processing order that must be preserved.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the specific workstation that must perform this task (must match one of the machine_ids). Indicates which layout desk, press, or binder the task needs.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Time required (in the chosen time unit) for the job to be processed at this stage on the required_machine_id; used to compute sequencing and the makespan.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total count of vessels (pots) in this batch that must each go through shaping, drying, and firing. This is the number of jobs to schedule.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of distinct studio stations (e.g., bench for shaping, drying area/rack, kiln) available and used in the shared processing order for every vessel.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifiers (names or IDs) for each vessel to be scheduled. Each identifier links the vessel to its sequence of three tasks (shape, dry, fire).

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifiers for the studio stations (e.g., 'bench', 'drying_rack', 'kiln') listed in the common processing order that every vessel follows.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The vessel identifier this task belongs to; matches one entry from the global vessel_list so all tasks can be grouped per pot.

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Index of the task within the vessel's sequence (1 = shaping on the bench, 2 = drying, 3 = firing in the kiln). This enforces the order each vessel must follow.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the required studio station for this task (must reference an entry from station_list), e.g., bench, drying_rack, or kiln.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Processing time required for this vessel at the specified station (duration of shaping, drying, or firing). Use the same time units as provided in the instance.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of devices (phones) in the batch that must each go through inspection, repair, and testing. This tells the solver how many jobs (devices) to schedule.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of distinct workstations (stations) in the shop; for this scenario it corresponds to the count of sequential stops (e.g., inspection, repair, testing). Each workstation can handle at most one device at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for each device (phone) to be repaired. These are the job labels the schedule must order and track through the three stations.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifiers for the workstations (e.g., inspection_station, repair_bench, test_rig). These labels indicate which physical station executes a task and are used to enforce that a station cannot process overlapping devices.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the device (phone) that this task belongs to; matches one entry from device_ids and groups that device's sequence of steps.

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Index of the processing step within the device's fixed sequence. In this scenario steps follow the same order for every device (1 = inspection, 2 = repair, 3 = testing), and the solver must respect this ordering when scheduling.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the workstation required for this step of the device. This indicates which station must be available to process the task and enforces that the station cannot run overlapping tasks for different devices.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Amount of time the device occupies the specified workstation for this step (in the instance's time units, e.g., minutes). Use this to compute start/finish times and the final makespan (time when the last device finishes testing).

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of bicycles (jobs) that must pass through the three service steps. This is the count of bikes to schedule so all finish inspection → adjustment → road check.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of distinct service bays (machines) available in the shop. Each bay represents a station (e.g., inspection bay, adjustment bay, road check bay) and can process at most one bike at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: An ordered list of identifiers for each bicycle to be serviced. Each identifier uniquely names a job whose tasks must follow the inspection → adjustment → road check sequence.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifiers for the service bays/stations in the shop. These correspond to the stations used by every bike in the same order (inspection, adjustment, road check).

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the bike that this task belongs to (matches one entry from bike_ids).

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The index of the service step within the bike's fixed sequence: 1 = inspection, 2 = adjustment, 3 = road check. Tasks must respect this order for each bike.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the service bay required for this task (matches one entry from bay_ids). Indicates which bay must perform the step for the bike; bays cannot handle overlapping bikes.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The processing time required for this bike at the specified bay for this service step (e.g., minutes). Used to allocate start/end times so bays are not double-booked and the overall completion time (makespan) is minimized.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of garments in this batch (e.g., shirts, dresses, coats). Each garment must pass through the three ordered stops: spot treatment, wash, and press.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of processing stations involved in the flow. In this dry-cleaner scenario these correspond to the processing stages (spot treatment, wash, press) or to distinct machines if multiple machines exist per stage.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of unique identifiers for each garment in the stack; these IDs are used to reference and sequence garments through the three processing stages.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the machines or stations that perform processing (e.g., specific spot-treatment unit, specific washer, specific press). Task entries refer to these IDs to indicate which machine will handle a step.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the garment for which this task is defined; must match one entry in garment_ids.

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Index of the processing step in the required sequence for every garment: 1 = spot (stain) treatment, 2 = wash/clean, 3 = press/finish. The same ordered stages apply to every garment.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the specific machine/station that must perform this task (must match one of station_ids). For a given stage_index, this selects which spotter/washer/presser handles the garment.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Amount of time the garment occupies the specified station for this task (e.g., minutes). While a garment is processed for this duration, that machine cannot process another garment.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct scenes that must go through the three-stage production pipeline (shooting → rough edit → color grading); used to size the scheduling instance.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of physical rooms/resources available across stages (e.g., shooting sets, editing suites, color grading rooms). This counts all machines/rooms referenced in task entries.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for each scene to schedule. Each identifier corresponds to one scene that must visit the three stages in the same order.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the available rooms/resources (shooting sets, editing suites, grading rooms). These identifiers are referenced by each task to indicate where it must be processed.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the scene this task belongs to; links the task to a particular scene in the shooting/editing/grading pipeline.

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Index of the stage in the scene's sequence (e.g., 0 = shooting, 1 = rough edit, 2 = color grading). All scenes share the same stage order.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the specific room or suite required for this task (for example, a particular camera set, editing suite, or grading room). No two tasks can use the same room at the same time.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Time required for the task on its required room (e.g., minutes or hours). This is the processing time the room must be occupied for that scene at that stage.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of student groups that must be scheduled to use the lab routine (each group follows the same sequence: setup, experiment, cleanup).

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of lab benches/stations available (these correspond to the ordered steps/stations every group visits, e.g., setup bench, experiment bench, cleanup bench).

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifiers for each student group to be scheduled (one entry per group).

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifiers for each bench/station in the fixed processing order (names or IDs for setup, experiment, cleanup benches).

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the student group that the specific task (step) belongs to.

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Index of the step within the group's routine (for example 1 = setup, 2 = run experiment, 3 = cleanup), indicating the sequence position.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the bench/station required for this step (which bench the group must occupy for this part of the routine).

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: How long that group takes to complete this step at the specified bench (the processing time for the step, in the same time units provided in the instance).

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of saplings in the batch to be processed through all stations. This is the count of jobs the schedule must cover.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of distinct workstations (processing stations) available in the nursery (e.g., potting, fertilizing, shading). All saplings follow the same ordered sequence of these stations.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for each sapling (each job). These IDs uniquely identify the plants that must pass through potting, fertilizing, and shading in sequence.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the workstations (e.g., ['potting','fertilizing','shading']) in the common processing order. These identifiers are referenced by each task to indicate where it must be processed.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the sapling (job) to which this task belongs. Used to link multiple ordered tasks (potting→fertilizing→shading) for the same plant.

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Index of the task within the sapling's required sequence (e.g., 1=potting, 2=fertilizing, 3=shading). Determines the intra-job order that must be respected when scheduling.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the specific workstation required for this task (must match one of the station_ids). A station can process at most one sapling at a time.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Time required for this sapling to be processed at the specified station (in consistent time units). These durations determine task lengths used to compute start/finish times and the overall makespan.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: The total count of pizzas to schedule during the shift. Each pizza is treated as one job that must pass through all stations in order.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of distinct work stations (shaping, topping, baking, etc.). Every station can handle at most one pizza at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: The identifiers for each pizza (job). These labels distinguish pies and determine their order in a candidate schedule.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: The identifiers for each station in the shop (e.g., shaping_counter, topping_table, oven). These are referenced by tasks to indicate where processing occurs.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the pizza this task belongs to (must match one of the pizza_ids).

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The sequence index of the step for that pizza (e.g., 1 = dough shaping, 2 = toppings, 3 = baking). Defines the required order of operations for the pizza.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The station where this step must be performed (must match one of the station_ids), such as the shaping area, topping station, or oven.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: How long the pizza occupies the required station for this step, expressed in the scheduling time unit (e.g., minutes). Used to compute start/end times and avoid overlaps at stations.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of customer vehicles that must be scheduled through the shop (each vehicle is a job that will visit the three service stages in sequence).

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of distinct service bays/stations available (e.g., inspection bay, repair bay, paint booth). These are the resources that cannot handle more than one vehicle at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifiers for each customer vehicle to be scheduled (the sequence in which these vehicles are ordered determines the shop's workflow and makespan).

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifiers for each service bay/station (each corresponds to a processing stage such as inspection, repair, or paint that vehicles must visit in the same order).

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the vehicle receiving the service step; links this task to a specific customer vehicle.

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Index of the service step within the vehicle's sequence (1 = first step, 2 = second, etc.), reflecting the required order: inspection, then repair, then paint.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the specific service bay required for this task (maps the step to the bay that must perform the work, e.g., inspection bay, repair bay, paint booth).

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Processing time required for this vehicle at the specified bay (time units for the service step). Used to compute start/finish times and the overall makespan.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of garments in the current batch that must each go through cutting, then stitching, then pressing.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of distinct physical workstations available in the shop (e.g., cutting tables, sewing machines, pressing stations).

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of identifiers for each garment piece in the batch (each identifier corresponds to one full garment that must be scheduled).

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifiers for each workstation in the shop (examples: 'cutting_table_1', 'sewing_machine_2', 'press_1'); these are referenced when assigning tasks to a specific station.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the garment this task belongs to; must match one entry from the garment_ids list.

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Index of the operation within the garment's fixed workflow (use the consistent order: 1 = cutting, 2 = stitching, 3 = pressing).

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the workstation that must perform this operation (must match one of the workstation_ids; indicates the cutting table, a particular sewing machine, or a specific press).

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Time required for this garment to be processed at the given workstation (in consistent time units, e.g., minutes); used to ensure no two garments occupy the same workstation simultaneously.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of patients to schedule for the day. Each patient is a separate job that must go through all clinic stages in order.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of sequential clinic stages every patient must pass through (for example: registration, scanning, review). This is the length of the common processing sequence.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of unique identifiers for each patient (job). These IDs are used to refer to each person's sequence of activities through the clinic.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifiers for the ordered stages (machines) in the clinic workflow, e.g. 'registration', 'scanner', 'review_room'. The order here defines the required processing order for every patient.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the patient this task belongs to (matches an entry from patient_ids).

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The position of this task within the patient's sequence (1..nr_stages). It indicates which step in the visit this is (first = sign-in/registration, second = scan, third = review, etc.).

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Which clinic stage (from stage_ids) is required for this task — e.g. a registration desk, a particular scanner, or a review room. A given stage cannot serve more than one patient at the same time.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The expected processing time (in minutes) that this patient will occupy the specified stage. Use these durations to compute start/finish times and the overall makespan.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of wood pieces (jobs) that must be processed through the shop; this is the count of items you must sequence so each goes through cutting, sanding, and varnishing.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of distinct work stations (machines) in the fixed processing flow — here the stations for cutting, sanding, varnishing — i.e., how many sequential operation locations exist.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifiers for each wood piece to be scheduled (e.g., piece IDs). The sequencing decision orders these pieces through the three operations.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifiers for each shop station (e.g., cutting_station, sanding_station, varnish_station). All pieces use these stations in the same fixed order.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the specific wood piece that a task belongs to; ties a task to its piece so the piece's tasks are executed in the fixed order.

job_task_item_fields.name: task_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Index of the operation within the piece's fixed sequence (e.g., 1 = cutting, 2 = sanding, 3 = varnishing); determines the per-piece order of tasks that must be respected.

job_task_item_fields.name: machine_id
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the specific shop station required for this operation (which station performs the operation indexed by task_id); indicates which station must be reserved for the task.

job_task_item_fields.name: duration
job_task_item_fields.scenario_description: Predetermined time the operation takes on its station (e.g., minutes). These fixed processing times are used to compute start/finish times and the overall makespan.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of furniture frames (jobs) that must be processed through the shop. The scheduler will plan these frames so each goes through cutting, assembly, and stitching in turn.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of work stations (machines) in the shared workflow. In this shop the stations correspond to the sequential steps (e.g., cutting, assembly, stitching); each station can handle at most one frame at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifiers for each frame to be scheduled (e.g., frame_1, frame_2). These are the job labels the schedule assigns start and end times to for each processing step.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifiers for the stations (machines) that perform steps in the common order (for example: 'cutting', 'assembly', 'stitching'). These label which station is required for a given task.

job_task_item_fields.name: job_id
